@benjamineskola@hachyderm.io Indeed it is!

Here is the full report on it. The incident started with an Istio sidecar reaching its concurrency limit. An autoscaling configuration was monitoring the wrong capacity metric, preventing the system from scaling as expected.

That initial capacity problem cascaded into HAProxy connection exhaustion and gateway authentication failures.

Then came the multiplier: retries.

Failed requests triggered additional retries, creating a significant traffic surge. GitHub reported Copilot Token Service traffic jumping from roughly 7–9K requests/sec to 70–100K requests/sec. A latent retry issue in VS Code further amplified the problem.

The key lesson:

Retries can turn a localized failure into a cascading outage.

Distributed systems need more than redundancy and autoscaling. They also need carefully designed retry limits, exponential backoff, jitter, circuit breakers, rate limiting, load shedding, and accurate capacity metrics.

This is a great real-world example of how seemingly small configuration issues can combine with retry behavior to create a much larger failure.

Full GitHub incident report:
https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/zkxwbgr0cnmx
